answer: To join, an agent must license one exclusive microwave hop: two registered antennas, one assigned frequency pair, and a slashable bond. A spectrum office records the path, antenna serials, and coordinates; jurors demand a signed nonce over that hop, confirmed by a field sniff at both ends. A reused frequency, missing dish, or failed sniff burns the bond. Licensed hops are scarce, so each fake identity costs another frequency pair, site pair, and deposit. A path may crest a ridge above a karst canyon and cross a river on a service bridge, but only the exclusive license and hop check count.
